place: Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands
setup: Sea 29–30 °C, abundant moisture; El Niño shifts typhoon genesis southeast, giving longer tracks over warm water.
trigger: Tropical storm 1,330 km east of Guam on 16 Oct; rapid intensification expected within ~36 h.
amplifiers: 6–12 in rain, 15–20 ft surf, 2–3 ft coastal inundation forecast for 18 Oct; shear 17–23 mph is the main brake.

setup: Third major hurricane in a month on this coast (Rachel, Simon, Trudy); record eastern Pacific season (ACE beyond 2018); Niño 1+2 +5.2 °C.
trigger: Cat 1 (80 kt) at 00 UTC 16 Oct to major (105 kt) by 15 UTC: ~+25 kt in 15 h. Then stalled: dry air opened the south eyewall; 110 mph, 963 mb by midday.
amplifiers: Low shear, deep ocean heat refills fast (Simon’s cold wake recovered in ~3 days); El Niño outweighs an unhelpful MJO phase 2.

place: Oklahoma, West Texas, Rockies, eastern US
type: Stalled front: flash flood, snow, freeze
setup: Record-warm air (Omaha four 90 °F days, OKC record heat), warm Gulf, moisture linked to Hurricane Simon, drought-hardened ground.
trigger: Front stalled between a slow Four Corners upper low and a Southeast ridge; 45 mph low-level jet fed training storms.
amplifiers: Record October precipitable water 2.23 in at Norman; 3–6 in OKC, 4–11 in by radar west; Canadian River major flood. Canadian high then shoved the front south after sunset: 20–25 °F drop, first freeze.
climate_signal: No study; warmer air holds ~7% more water per °C (physical reasoning). El Niño link indirect, via Simon moisture.

setup: Warm but not record sea: eastern Mediterranean 24.3 °C, +0.98 °C on 1 Oct (MED_OISST).
trigger: Slow, electrically intense thunderstorm clusters; synoptic system not yet described by met services.
amplifiers: Istanbul: heaviest since records began in 1942, 193.8 mm at Ömerli; Rhodes 264 mm (202 mm in 6 h 20 min). Steep catchments, urban culverts, basements.

event: Kelvin wave and California high water
setup: Collapsed trade winds (central Pacific −3.0) sent warm water east; a coastally trapped Kelvin wave is moving north at ~6 mph.
trigger: Kelvin wave 9–12 in on top of marine heatwave expansion 6–10 in and sea-level rise 2–3 in: water 1–2 ft above tide predictions.
amplifiers: Damage in Long Beach, Balboa Peninsula inundated, San Clemente erosion. King tides 24–26 Nov, 22–25 Dec, 20–23 Jan expected 1–2 ft above predictions.
climate_signal: Long-term sea-level rise adds 2–3 in plus 6–8 in already in the tidal datum (Swain).

setup: Record El Niño: eastern Pacific season energy 323 vs 121 normal.
trigger: Tropical wave over 30–31 °C water at 18–20°N.
amplifiers: Cat 1 to Cat 4 in ~24 h (+50 mph; RI threshold +35). Shear only 8–12 kt, moist mid-levels (RH 84–100%).
climate_signal: No study; warmer oceans raise the ceiling for rapid intensification (physical reasoning).

setup: Wet end of monsoon: ~430 mm on 18–27 Sep, then 43 mm on 7–9 Oct (model data).
trigger: ~1 km landslide at Siringe Himal dammed the Ungilung stream; breach ~04:00 11 Oct.
amplifiers: Saturated steep slopes in the 2015 earthquake region; unmonitored tributary.
climate_signal: See Langtang: warming loads high slopes with rain and meltwater.

setup: 28–29 °C water off Baja kept the storm alive far north.
trigger: Long-period south swell aimed at south-facing beaches.
amplifiers: Water already 1–2 ft above tide predictions (marine heatwave 6–10 in + coastally trapped Kelvin wave 9–12 in); new-moon spring tides (10 Oct); third surf event in five weeks after Marie and Polo.

setup: Record summer Mediterranean heat; sea 25.7 °C on 3 Oct.
trigger: Upper trough from the west: 500 hPa heights fell 5,825 to 5,687 m.
amplifiers: CAPE 1,850–2,280 J/kg; short steep volcanic torrents through built-up channels. Models gave only ~5 mm/h.
climate_signal: No study; warmer sea feeds autumn storms (physical reasoning).

setup: El Niño shear suppresses the Atlantic (17% of normal energy); the Gulf is the exception.
trigger: Low over the southern Gulf ~7 Oct, MJO phases 1–2 favourable.
amplifiers: Gulf water 28–29.5 °C; shear ~20 kt. Capped by rising shear (27–39 kt) and dry air before landfall as Cat 2.

setup: Weekly Niño 3.4 +3.3 °C (7 Oct), relative +2.4; Niño 1+2 +5.2; heat content +3.39 °C; official ONI (Jul–Sep) +2.16.
trigger: ENSO Longitude Index 191.5°E, the easternmost on record: an east-based event like 1982–83 and 1997–98.
amplifiers: California: >90% odds of a wetter-than-average winter, peak Dec–Mar (Swain). Quoted "ONI +3.3" is a weekly value, not the official ONI.
climate_signal: California emergency proclamation cites a study finding El Niño events now 36% stronger than pre-industrial.

setup: ENFEN alert (16 Sep): coastal El Niño of extraordinary magnitude likely; coastal sea 5–8 °C above normal.
trigger: Kelvin waves reaching South America keep warm water against the coast.
amplifiers: Anchovy season ended at 25% of quota; early heavy rain in Tumbes and Piura; heaviest rain expected Feb–Mar 2027.

setup: Warm central Pacific during the record El Niño.
trigger: Category 5 on 2 Sep; ridge weakened 5 Sep and an upper low pulled it north (Iniki-like track).
amplifiers: Passed 60 miles from Kauaʻi as Cat 2: gusts 92 mph, 21.1 in rain, surge; track shifted 10–15 miles east of forecast.

setup: Very warm Jul–Aug; more rain than snow; freezing level up ~100 m/decade; glacier retreat 1–2.3%/yr.
trigger: ~2 km² of rock and ice fell 1,400 m from 5,150 m (energy like M5.5).
amplifiers: Became a debris flood at ~188 km/h; 5,850 m³/s at Devghat; 30.5 million m³ of debris.
climate_signal: Warming raised local Jul–Aug heat ~1.5 °C; geology the root cause (WWA).

setup: Dry April–June, successive heatwaves; hottest June–July on record.
trigger: Persistent alternating highs and lows (WMO).
amplifiers: Dry soils intensified heat; fires in SW France and Spain; western Mediterranean up to 6 °C above normal.
climate_signal: ~2 °C of Mediterranean warming is human-caused; marine heat virtually impossible pre-industrial (WWA).

setup: Season started below average.
trigger: Prolonged July heat and dryness, lightning outbreak week of 20 Jul.
amplifiers: 94% of 3M+ ha burned late Jun–late Jul; smoke reached 120M people.

event: US Fourth of July heat dome
setup: Pronounced upper ridge over the eastern US.
trigger: Ridge drew humid Gulf air; lasted over a week.
amplifiers: Heat index 105–115 °F; record 5-day heat stress.

setup: Near-record-dry soils after record May heat.
trigger: Persistent high with southerly flow from North Africa.
amplifiers: 5–12 °C above normal; 43.3 °C in France.
climate_signal: 3.5 °C hotter by day than the same pattern in 1976 (WWA).

setup: Early Feb–Mar heat, drought.
trigger: Heat built mid-April after western disturbances ended.
amplifiers: Above 46 °C in many cities; record power demand.

setup: Strong slow-moving ridge.
trigger: Clear skies, sinking air; LA extreme heat warning.
amplifiers: 11–17 °C above normal; Phoenix ~41 °C vs March record 38 °C.
climate_signal: Virtually impossible without warming; ~800× more likely, +2.6 °C (WWA).

setup: Deep tropical moisture.
trigger: Back-to-back lows and upper disturbances reversed the trades.
amplifiers: Rain almost daily for two weeks, lifted by mountains: 54.92 in on Maui; >$1B damage.

setup: Wet rainy season.
trigger: Persistent localised rain; wettest February since 1961 in Juiz de Fora.
amplifiers: Unplanned homes on steep slopes; ~130,000 in high-risk zones; sirens did not reach all.

setup: Stretched polar vortex sent Arctic air south.
trigger: Pacific low crossed the Plains, drew Gulf moisture, re-formed as a nor'easter.
amplifiers: Up to 1 in ice, 1–2 ft snow, 1M+ without power; 46 cm in Toronto.

setup: Blocking high to the north.
trigger: Cut-off low over Iberia stalled for a week.
amplifiers: 206 mm in Tunisia, ~10 m waves off Spain; boats capsized after leaving Sfax.

setup: Weak La Niña and warm seas.
trigger: Repeated heavy rain systems; a year's rain in days in places.
amplifiers: Moisture-rich air; rivers burst, Kruger closed.
